stem: Which condition is associated with components of the extracellular matrix?
rationale: Certain components of the ECM are involved in rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BIOMEDICAL IMPORTANCE

stem: In which structure is type XV collagen typically found?
rationale: Type XV collagen is associated with collagens close to basement membranes in many tissues, including the eye, muscle, and microvessels.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGEN IS THE MOST ABUNDANT PROTEIN IN THE ANIMAL WORLD

stem: In which structure is type II collagen typically found?
rationale: Type II collagen is present in cartilage and the vitreous humor.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGEN IS THE MOST ABUNDANT PROTEIN IN THE ANIMAL WORLD

stem: In which structure is type III collagen typically found?
rationale: Type III collagen is located in extensible connective tissues, such as skin, lung, and the vascular system.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGEN IS THE MOST ABUNDANT PROTEIN IN THE ANIMAL WORLD

stem: Glycine requires which substance?
rationale: Glycine residues occur at every third position of the triple helical portion of the alpha chain. Glycine is the only amino acid small enough to be accommodated in the limited space available in the central core of the triple helix. The repeating structure (Gly-X-Y)n is an absolute requirement for the formation of the triple helix.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE

stem: Which substrate does lysyl hydroxylase act on?
rationale: Lysyl hydroxylase modifies lysines to hydroxylysine. Lysyl hydroxylase has similar cofactors to prolyl hydroxylase.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE

stem: Which substrate does lysyl oxidase act on?
rationale: After secretion from the cell, certain lysyl residues of tropoelastin are oxidatively deaminated to aldehydes by lysyl oxidase.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > ELASTIN CONFERS EXTENSIBILITY & RECOIL

stem: What substance is lysine converted into by lysyl oxidase?
rationale: Covalent cross-links form through the action of lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme that oxidatively deaminates the \(ε\) -amino groups of certain lysine and hydroxylysine residues, yielding reactive aldehydes.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE

stem: What substance is hydroxylysine converted into by lysyl oxidase?
rationale: Covalent cross-links form through the action of lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme that oxidatively deaminates the \(ε\) -amino groups of certain lysine and hydroxylysine residues, yielding reactive aldehydes.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE

stem: Procollagen is converted into which substance?
rationale: The polypeptide extensions in procollagen are not present in mature collagen.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > Collagen Undergoes Extensive Posttranslational Modifications

stem: What substance is collagen converted into after the removal of propeptides?
rationale: The removal of propeptides forms the monomeric units of collagen, termed tropocollagen.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > Extracellular

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of chondrodysplasias?
rationale: Mutations in COL2A1 can lead to severe chondrodysplasia.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of osteogenesis imperfecta?
rationale: Types I to IV of osteogenesis imperfecta are caused by mutations in the COL1A1 or COL1A2 genes or both. Type I osteogenesis imperfecta is mild.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of osteoporosis?
rationale: Mutations in COL1A1 can lead to osteoporosis.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome?
rationale: Mutations in Tenascin XB (TNXB) can lead to classical-like Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (cLEDS).
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of osteoarthritis?
rationale: Mutations in COL2A1 can lead to osteoarthritis.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Alport syndrome?
rationale: Mutations in COL4A3 can lead to Alport syndrome (autosomal and X-linked).
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia?
rationale: Mutations in COL10A1 can lead to Schmid metaphyseal chondrodysplasia.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Menkes disease?
rationale: Mutations in ATP7A can lead to Menkes disease.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of classical-like Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (cEDS)?
rationale: The classical-like EDS (cEDS) involves defects in Tenascin XB (TNXB). The classical-like EDS (cEDS) has an incidence of less than 1:1,000,000.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of myopathic EDS?
rationale: The myopathic EDS (mEDS) involves defects in type XII collagen. The myopathic EDS (mEDS) has an incidence of less than 1:1,000,000.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of epidermolysis bullosa?
rationale: Epidermolysis bullosa is a condition where the skin breaks and blisters as a result of minor trauma.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: Ascorbic acid requires which substance?
rationale: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases require ascorbic acid as a cofactor.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > COLLAGENS HAVE A TRIPLE HELIX STRUCTURE > A Number of Genetic & Deficiency Diseases Result From Abnormalities in the Synthesis of Collagen

stem: In which structure is elastin found in large amounts?
rationale: Elastin is present in large amounts in large arterial blood vessels.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > ELASTIN CONFERS EXTENSIBILITY & RECOIL

stem: What is the soluble monomer form of elastin called?
rationale: Elastin is synthesized as a soluble monomer of approximately 70 kDa called tropoelastin.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > ELASTIN CONFERS EXTENSIBILITY & RECOIL

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of pulmonary emphysema?
rationale: Fragmentation or a decrease of elastin is found in conditions such as pulmonary emphysema.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > ELASTIN CONFERS EXTENSIBILITY & RECOIL

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of dermatosparaxis?
rationale: Fragmentation or a decrease of elastin is found in conditions such as cutis laxa.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > ELASTIN CONFERS EXTENSIBILITY & RECOIL

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Marfan syndrome?
rationale: Most cases of Marfan syndrome are caused by mutations in the gene for fibrillin-1.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > FIBRILLINS ARE STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF MICROFIBRILS > Marfan Syndrome Is Caused by Mutations in the Gene for Fibrillin-1

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of acromicric dysplasia?
rationale: Mutations in the fibrillin-1 gene have also been identified as the cause of acromicric dysplasia.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > FIBRILLINS ARE STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS OF MICROFIBRILS > Marfan Syndrome Is Caused by Mutations in the Gene for Fibrillin-1

stem: Which structure does laminin form networks in?
rationale: Laminin forms networks in basal laminas.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS

stem: In which structure is heparan sulfate found?
rationale: Although some plasma proteins, such as albumin, are smaller than the pore size, they are prevented from passing through by the negative charges of heparan sulfate and certain sialic acid-containing glycoproteins present in the lamina.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS

stem: In which structure are sialic acid-containing glycoproteins found?
rationale: Although some plasma proteins, such as albumin, are smaller than the pore size, they are prevented from passing through by the negative charges of heparan sulfate and certain sialic acid-containing glycoproteins present in the lamina.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of albuminuria?
rationale: Damage to the normal structure of the glomerulus can result in severe albuminuria, with relatively massive amounts of albumin and certain other plasma proteins passing through into the urine.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS

stem: GlcUA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Modifications also involve the epimerization of GlcUA to IdUA residues.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Further Modifications

stem: In which structure are proteoglycans mainly found?
rationale: Proteoglycans are mainly located in the extracellular matrix or ground substance.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Proteoglycans Are Important in the Structural Organization of the Extracellular Matrix

stem: In which structure is keratan sulfate found?
rationale: Keratan sulfate I and II are located in the cornea, cartilage, and loose connective tissue.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Various Glycosaminoglycans Exhibit Differences in Structure & Have Diverse Functions

stem: Which substance is transported by heparin?
rationale: Heparin is released into the blood from capillary walls by the action of lipoprotein lipase.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Heparin

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of mental retardation?
rationale: Hunter syndrome causes mental retardation.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Deficiencies of Enzymes That Degrade Glycosaminoglycans Result in Mucopolysaccharidoses

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Sanfilippo syndrome B?
rationale: A genetic defect in hyaluronidase causes MPS IX (Natowicz syndrome).
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Deficiencies of Enzymes That Degrade Glycosaminoglycans Result in Mucopolysaccharidoses

stem: Hyaluronidase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Hyaluronidase is an important enzyme involved in the catabolism of both hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Deficiencies of Enzymes That Degrade Glycosaminoglycans Result in Mucopolysaccharidoses

stem: Dermatan sulfate is a risk factor for which condition?
rationale: Dermatan sulfate may play a role in the development of atherosclerotic plaques.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > LAMININ IS A MAJOR PROTEIN COMPONENT OF BASAL LAMINAS > Proteoglycans Are Associated With Major Diseases & Aging

stem: Noncollagen proteins are found within which structure?
rationale: Noncollagen proteins are a category of proteins found in bone.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: Plasma proteins are found within which structure?
rationale: Plasma proteins are a mixture of various plasma proteins found in bone.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: BMPs are found within which structure?
rationale: Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) are a family of at least 20 secreted proteins with a variety of actions on bone, many of which induce ectopic bone growth.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: Bone requires which substance for its strength and resilience?
rationale: Approximately 99% of the body's calcium is contained in bone. Hydroxyapatite confers on bone the strength and resilience required for its physiologic roles.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: Osteocytes are found within which structure?
rationale: Osteocytes are found in mature bone. Osteocytes are involved in the maintenance of the bone matrix.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: Cortical is part of which structure?
rationale: Bone consists of two types of tissue: trabecular (cancellous or spongy) bone and compact (cortical) bone.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: The cortex is part of which structure?
rationale: Compact bone forms the cortex (or outer shell) of most bones. Compact bone accounts for about 80% of the weight of the human skeleton.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS A MINERALIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE

stem: The sclera is part of which structure?
rationale: The sclera of the eye in osteogenesis imperfecta is often abnormally thin and translucent. The sclera of the eye in osteogenesis imperfecta appears blue due to a deficiency of connective tissue.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Glycine is converted into which substance?
rationale: The replacement of glycine by another bulkier amino acid affects the formation of the collagen triple helix. Mutations in the COL1A1 and COL1A2 genes generally result in decreased expression of collagen.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Pfeiffer syndrome?
rationale: Pfeiffer, Jackson-Weiss, and Crouzon syndromes are caused by mutations in the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) 1 and/or 2.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of Crouzon syndrome?
rationale: Pfeiffer, Jackson-Weiss, and Crouzon syndromes are caused by mutations in the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) 1 and/or 2.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of craniosynostosis?
rationale: In the Pfeiffer, Jackson-Weiss, and Crouzon syndromes, there is premature fusion of some bones in the skull, known as craniosynostosis.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of rickets?
rationale: Rickets is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D in childhood.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of osteomalacia?
rationale: Osteomalacia is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D in adults.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hyperparathyroidism?
rationale: Hyperparathyroidism is caused by excess parathyroid hormone leading to bone resorption.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > BONE IS AFFECTED BY MANY METABOLIC & GENETIC DISORDERS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of achondroplasia?
rationale: Achondroplasia is due to mutations in the gene encoding fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3).
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > CHONDRODYSPLASIAS ARE HEREDITARY DISORDERS AFFECTING CARTILAGE

stem: Which substance is synthesised by chondrocytes in cartilage?
rationale: Various proteases, such as collagenases and stromelysin, synthesized by chondrocytes can degrade collagen and other proteins in cartilage. Chondronectin is involved in the attachment of type II collagen to chondrocytes (cartilage cells).
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > THE MAJOR COMPONENTS OF CARTILAGE ARE TYPE II COLLAGEN & CERTAIN PROTEOGLYCANS

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hypochondroplasia?
rationale: Mutations in the FGFR3 gene can result in hypochondroplasia.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > CHONDRODYSPLASIAS ARE HEREDITARY DISORDERS AFFECTING CARTILAGE

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of SADDAN?
rationale: Mutations in the FGFR3 gene can lead to the SADDAN phenotype.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > CHONDRODYSPLASIAS ARE HEREDITARY DISORDERS AFFECTING CARTILAGE

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of diastrophic dysplasia?
rationale: Diastrophic dysplasia is due to mutation in a sulfate transporter.
citation: chapter_49_the_extracellular_matrix — Overview > CHONDRODYSPLASIAS ARE HEREDITARY DISORDERS AFFECTING CARTILAGE
